title: Prudential Standard SPS 530 Investment Governance

summary: SPS 530 requires every RSE licensee to have a Board-overseen investment governance framework: specific and measurable return and risk objectives for each investment option, documented investment strategies that address the SIS Act s52(6) factors and diversification, due diligence before selecting investments, independent performance monitoring against benchmarks, at least annual strategy reviews, a Board-approved investment stress testing program, a liquidity management plan, and a valuation governance framework with a Board-approved valuation policy.

clauses.heading: Board responsibilities
clauses.text: The RSE licensee is ultimately responsible for the sound and prudent management of each RSE's investments (paragraph 7). The Board must at least approve investment objectives for each option and an investment strategy for each RSE and option consistent with SIS Act s52(6) and (13), monitor whether objectives are met, and act on investment reports.

clauses.heading: Investment governance framework
clauses.text: An RSE licensee must at all times have an investment governance framework, for which the Board is ultimately responsible (paragraph 12). Paragraph 13 lists its minimum content: objectives per option, a reporting measures methodology, investment strategies, Board investment policies, role statements, processes for performance and risk measurement, stress testing, valuation and reporting, and a review process.

clauses.section_name: Review of the investment governance framework
clauses.heading: Three-yearly independent review
clauses.text: The framework's appropriateness, effectiveness and adequacy must be comprehensively reviewed at least every three years by operationally independent, appropriately trained and competent persons.

clauses.heading: Investment objectives
clauses.text: When formulating each option's strategy, the RSE licensee must set objectives aligned to the RSE's size, business mix and complexity that are specific and measurable and include at least a return objective and a risk objective.

clauses.heading: Documenting the investment strategy and diversification
clauses.text: For each strategy the RSE licensee must document how it had regard to each SIS Act s52(6) factor (paragraph 19), analyse risk factors, sources of return and their interaction when setting diversification (paragraph 20), and set asset allocation targets, ranges and a rebalancing policy for multi-asset options (paragraph 21). MySuper strategies need further documentation (paragraph 22).

clauses.section_name: Giving effect to the investment strategy
clauses.heading: Investment selection due diligence
clauses.text: An RSE licensee must have an investment selection process with due diligence commensurate with each investment before selection, ensuring it understands the investment, how it performs under stress scenarios, and that it is appropriate for the option (paragraph 24).

clauses.heading: Performance monitoring
clauses.text: An RSE licensee must set measures and benchmarks to monitor each MySuper product, option and investment, with Board approval of measures other than investment-level benchmarks (paragraph 25), report performance and its drivers regularly to the Board and senior management (paragraph 26), and keep performance assessors operationally independent of those making the investments (paragraph 27).

clauses.heading: Annual strategy review
clauses.text: Each strategy must have a Board-approved review policy requiring review against objectives at least annually, with triggers for interim reviews, reporting of results to the Board and criteria for change. Board decisions to amend a strategy must be supported by sufficient justification and analysis (paragraph 29).

clauses.heading: Investment stress testing program
clauses.text: An RSE licensee must have a Board-approved, comprehensive investment stress testing program integrated into its framework, with adverse scenarios for each option (paragraph 31), testing before implementation and at least annually (paragraph 32), documented methodology and roles (paragraph 33), and results reviewed by the Board and reflected in the framework (paragraphs 34 and 35).

clauses.heading: Liquidity management plan
clauses.text: An RSE licensee must have a Board-approved liquidity management plan for each RSE covering every option, ongoing measurement and management, liquidity under stress, defined liquidity events and responses, roles, and key metrics reported to the Board. Liquidity stress testing must form part of the stress testing program (paragraph 38).

clauses.heading: Valuation governance
clauses.text: An RSE licensee must have an adequate valuation governance framework to identify and manage valuation risk, including a Board-approved valuation policy covering roles, reporting, methodologies by asset class, external valuations, valuation frequency, interim valuation triggers, back-testing and dispute escalation (paragraph 40).
